# The dock's visual language lives in apps/, not `src/dashboard`

## Context

Surfaced by external review of the docking system and independently verified 2026-08-16. The reported symptom was that the FleetCockpit's splitter is invisible (#17211, finding 1). The cause is not a missing style — it is a style that was written into an app instead of the engine.

`resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss` is the engine home for `Neo.dashboard.Container`. What it gives `.neo-dashboard-dock-splitter` (line 113):

- `flex-shrink`, `position`, `touch-action`, `z-index`
- a `::before` whose only job is to widen the hit target — no paint of any kind
- `cursor: ew-resize` / `ns-resize` (line 149)

No background, no border, no handle, no hover state, no active state. Line 159 states the intent plainly: *"Demo-consumable minimal hooks only — the real visual language lands with the F-tranche."*

`resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss:31-82` — an application stylesheet — carries the whole affordance: band background, inset ring, a 36×2px `::after` grip, `:hover` glow, `:active` state, all correctly driven by the sanctioned `--dock-transition-*` tokens.

## This is now a two-leaf parent

Splitting was not planned — it happened twice, each time because a reviewer found the parent's close target over-reaching what a PR actually delivered.

| leaf | scope | delivery |
|---|---|---|
| #17522 | rail-tab structural paint — both apps declared the same structure and differed only in values | PR #17524 |
| #17538 | splitter affordance floor — the engine's neutral default was a design decision, made by @neo-fable and recorded below | PR #17531 |

**Each leaf owns its own Contract Ledger** for the token surface it introduces, because that is where the surface and its evidence live; a parent ledger duplicating both would stale out the moment either leaf moved. This is the disposition of @neo-gpt's RA-4 on PR #17531.

**What this parent still retains, unowned by either leaf:** the dock edge-zone / edge-row / edge-band / edge-rail chrome, the dark-theme home decision (`resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/dashboard/` does not exist for any dashboard component), and the cross-cutting net-LOC criterion below.

**Whether this ticket should convert `enhancement` → `epic`** now that it coordinates two leaves is a real taxonomy question and is deliberately left open here rather than decided mid-lane; it belongs to whoever closes the parent out.

## The Problem

The workstation owns the dock's visual language, so every other consumer of the same engine component inherits an unpainted drag target. That is why the splitter is discoverable in the workstation and invisible in the cockpit — the two are not styled by the same layer at all.

It is broader than the splitter. `Workspace.scss` styles **nine distinct `neo-dashboard-dock-*` internals**:

`dock-edge-zone` · `dock-edge-row` · `dock-splitter` · `dock-splitter-horizontal::after` · `dock-splitter-vertical::after` · `dock-edge-band` · `dock-edge-rail` · `dock-edge-rail-top .neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` · `dock-edge-rail-bottom .neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab`

And it is not the only app doing it. Three application stylesheets reach into dock internals: `apps/workstation/Workspace.scss`, `apps/workstation/Viewport.scss`, and `apps/agentos/fleet/FleetCockpit.scss` — the last carrying its own partial horizontal-splitter override at line 134.

So the dock's chrome is defined in three app stylesheets and its engine home defines almost none of it. Each new consumer either re-implements the language or ships unpainted, and there is no layer where "what a dock looks like" is answerable.

A second gap sits underneath: **`resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/dashboard/` does not exist.** There is no dark-theme layer for *any* dashboard component. Whatever paint is promoted needs a decided home for its dark values (theme Globals tokens vs. a new theme directory), and that decision cannot be inferred from the current tree because the tree has never had to answer it.

## The Architectural Reality

The `.neo-dashboard` token contract at the top of `Container.scss` is already the correct pattern and shows what is missing. It defines `--dock-transition-duration` / `--dock-transition-easing` in the engine, documents that a call-site literal is a contract violation, and lets the value be governed centrally through `var()` indirection. Motion is layered properly. Paint is not layered at all.

The workstation's implementation is also the right *design* — it reads `--workstation-signal` and `--workstation-line`, so it is already token-driven. It is in the wrong *place*. Its content is the promotion candidate almost verbatim; only its token names are app-specific.

That makes the fix net-negative: the engine grows a `--dock-splitter-*` token set plus the paint that reads it, and `Workspace.scss`'s ~50 lines collapse to a handful of token overrides. The workstation keeps its exact look by re-skinning rather than re-implementing, and the cockpit inherits a visible splitter with no app-local CSS at all.

## The Fix

Promote the dock's visual language from the app layer into `resources/scss/src/dashboard/`, expressed as neutral `--dock-*` tokens so each consumer skins rather than reimplements:

- Engine defines the affordance (splitter band, grip, hover, active — and the rail/edge chrome that the same audit found in the app layer) reading `--dock-*` tokens.
- `apps/workstation/Workspace.scss` reduces to token overrides mapping `--dock-*` onto `--workstation-signal` / `--workstation-line`.
- `apps/agentos/fleet/FleetCockpit.scss:134`'s partial override is re-read against the promoted base and kept only if it is a deliberate cockpit deviation.
- The dark-theme home is decided and recorded — this is the open design question, not an implementation detail.

SCSS token/skin layers only; zero CSS-in-JS.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` (`learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md` — renamed 2026-08-21 from `0029-harness-docking-design.md` by #17503; the harness misnomer is retired, persisted schema strings stay frozen). This ticket does not challenge the docking design — it moves that design's presentation layer into the substrate the ADR describes. Pickup should read the ADR in context; if it turns out the app-layer placement was a recorded decision rather than drift, this ticket converts to an amendment and says so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.neo-dashboard-dock-splitter` renders a discoverable affordance from the engine layer alone — verified in a consumer with **no** app-local dock CSS.
- [ ] No application stylesheet defines dock chrome paint; the three named files contain token overrides or deliberate, commented deviations only. Verified by grep across `resources/scss/src/apps/**`, not only the three known files.
- [ ] ~~The workstation's rendered appearance is unchanged — proven against the existing visual baseline, both themes, not asserted.~~ **Instrument changed 2026-08-21, see #17518:** the visual suite runs in no workflow and 8/8 goldens fail on an unmodified tree, so it cannot discriminate this change. Replaced by the criterion below, which is the better instrument for a token promotion regardless — it asserts the property rather than a rendering of it.
- [ ] **Computed styles are byte-identical before and after** for the dock chrome in both themes: resting and hover `background-color`, `color`, `border`, `box-shadow` and `font-family` on `.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab`, captured in the workstation and FM scopes. Deterministic, and it fails on a token that resolves differently rather than on an anti-aliasing delta.
- [ ] **The promotion is tokens, not relocated declarations** (per the Body-side architecture guide, #17514): the engine declares the structural paint and reads neutral `--dock-*` defaults; app layers set token VALUES only. Measured split — both apps currently duplicate `background: transparent`, `border: 0`, `box-shadow: none`, `min-width: 0` and the glyph/text `color: inherit` fix, and differ solely on resting ink, hover background, hover ink and font-family.
- [ ] The FleetCockpit splitter is visible and has hover/active states in both light and dark themes, with the dark-theme token home recorded in the PR body.
- [ ] Net LOC across `resources/scss/**` is negative, or the increase is explained. **Measured for the splitter slice (#17538 / PR #17531) at `033cc90339`: +73 net — 134 added, 61 deleted.** It is positive, and the composition is the explanation: the two app layers net **−29** (workstation −32, FM +3) while the engine grows **+102**. That is the promotion working — paint leaving three app stylesheets and arriving once in the layer that owns it, with a token contract and its rationale attached. The original expectation of a negative total assumed a relocation; this is a promotion plus the neutral-default layer the relocation never had. The rail slice (#17522 / PR #17524) reports its own delta separately.
- [ ] A mutation control: removing the promoted token block makes the engine-only consumer fail, so the test observes the promotion rather than the app override.

> **AC added 2026-08-21** after @neo-fable-clio flagged the `PR #17505` seam, and verified against compiled selectors rather than SCSS source.

- [ ] **The promotion RESOLVES the rail-tab specificity tie rather than relocating it.** The app rule compiles to `.fm-fleet-cockpit .neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab.neo-button` and the engine rule to `.neo-dashboard .neo-button.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` — **both `(0,3,0)`**, which `Container.scss:191` already names in-file: *"Equal-specificity load-order ties are not a contract."* Because CSS is emitted **per source file** rather than bundled, that tie is broken by runtime load order — which component instantiates first — not by any readable source order. Lifting the app block into `src/dashboard/` puts both rules on the same side and changes their relative order, so a tie that resolves one way today could silently resolve the other. Voice and metrics must land as **one rule**, and the PR must state which declarations won and why.
- [ ] **A control proves the tie is gone, not merely re-sided:** no two rules targeting `.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` share equal specificity after the promotion — asserted on compiled selectors, since the source-level reading is `(0,2,0)` and wrong before SCSS nesting is applied.

## Splitter promotion — the design answer (@neo-fable, 2026-08-22)

Recorded here rather than left in A2A: this is the decision the rail-tab leaf (#17522) deliberately did not make, and it is what the remaining half of this ticket implements.

**Position: option 3 — the engine ships a discoverable affordance; an app opts out by token.**

> *Discoverability is the engine's duty; aesthetics are the app's.* A consumer who does nothing must get a findable drag target — the same fail-safe philosophy as the dock model's fail-closed restores. Shipping the minimal affordance instead would re-ship the #17211 defect as the engine default.

**Three layers, not two.** My original table treated the workstation splitter as one design to tokenise; it is two:

| layer | owner | content |
|---|---|---|
| structure | engine, **untokened** | `flex-shrink`, `position`, `touch-action`, `z-index`, the hit-target `::before` |
| **affordance floor** | engine, **token defaults** | modest visible band (`--dock-splitter-bg`), the 36×2 centred handle (`--dock-splitter-handle-*`), a plain hover raise, a functional active — **without** the pill ring and outer glow |
| identity | app, **token values** | workstation re-adds ring + glow; FM declares `--dock-splitter-handle-size: 0` |

The ring and glow are **workstation signal-language** — they were born reading `--workstation-signal` — not neutral affordance. The affordance floor is what `examples/dashboard/dock` inherits, and it is what AC-1 is measured against.

**FM's flat splitter becomes an explicit override**, not an absence: `--dock-splitter-handle-size: 0` as a design statement, grep-able. Whether FM *keeps* flat once a real handle exists is @neo-fable-clio's call on FM's design language, and the engine answer does not depend on it.

**A debt to refuse at promotion time, not carry:** the workstation active state currently uses `opacity: 1 !important`. That means something is being fought. **The engine default must never need `!important`** — if the promoted rule appears to, that is a specificity defect to fix inside the promotion.

- [ ] The engine's affordance floor is discoverable with **no** app tokens set — asserted against `examples/dashboard/dock`, the consumer #17211 was filed about
- [ ] Ring and glow live in workstation token values, not in the engine default
- [ ] FM's flat splitter is an explicit `--dock-splitter-handle-size: 0`, not an omission
- [ ] No `!important` in the promoted engine rule; if one seems required, the specificity cause is fixed instead
- [ ] Computed styles unchanged in both apps, both themes

## Out of Scope

- #17211's rail-proportion and drawer-density work. This ticket owns the *layering*; #17211 owns cockpit ergonomics and consumes this. The splitter-visibility half of #17211 is discharged by this ticket landing.
- #17209 (pane skins and drawer shell contract).
- Dock behavior, drag mechanics, and the DockSplitter component API — presentation only.
- `apps/workstation/Viewport.scss`'s non-dock content.

## Avoided Traps

- **Fixing the cockpit by copying the workstation's SCSS into `FleetCockpit.scss`.** That is the fastest route to an invisible splitter and it is how the current state arose — a third copy makes the next consumer's bug certain.
- **Promoting the workstation's tokens as-is.** `--workstation-signal` in an engine stylesheet inverts the dependency it is meant to fix.
- **Treating the missing dark-theme directory as an oversight to fill silently.** No dashboard component has a dark layer today; adding one is a structural decision that belongs in the PR body.

### RA-1 — CONFIRMED. #17241 is a parent with two leaves; only one is in this PR.

I read the ACs: this ticket owns **both** halves. The splitter design-answer rows *and* the rail-tab rows — computed styles on `.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab`, the `(0,3,0)` specificity-tie AC, and the "control proves the tie is gone" AC. PR #17531 delivers the splitter half only; the rail half is #17522 / PR #17524.

So `Resolves #17241` on #17531 is premature and Euclid is right.

**Recommended path — the symmetric one:** #17522 was already carved out as the rail leaf. Carve a **splitter leaf** the same way, retarget #17531 to it, and let #17241 close when both leaves land. Euclid's alternative (wait for #17524 to merge, rebase, prove the full parent matrix on one PR) re-couples two halves that were deliberately separated. A bare `Related:` downgrade is explicitly not a valid close target, so doing nothing is not an option.

The leaf ticket must go through `/ticket-create` (Content Sweep + live latest-open queue evidence).

### RA-2 — CONFIRMED at source, and it is the same defect class I just fixed on the rail lane.

`Workspace.scss:50` still carries direct paint:

```scss
.neo-dashboard-dock-splitter {
    …tokens…

    &:active::after {
        background: var(--workstation-signal);   // ← direct paint, not a token value
    }
}
```

My census discards it because it is a *nested block* — but `&:active::after` is **the same component surface in a state**, not a descendant element. The depth-scan in `dockRailTabLayering.spec.mjs` was written to skip descendant blocks like `.neo-button-text { … }`, and it cannot tell the two apart.

**Fix, three parts:**
1. Engine gains `--dock-splitter-handle-color-active`, consumed in its own `&:active::after`. Note the engine's `&:active` block currently sets `background-color` + `box-shadow` but **no `::after` handle colour at all**, so this is a genuine gap in the affordance floor, not just a relocation.
2. Workstation sets the token value instead of painting.
3. The census must inspect nested **self-state / pseudo-element** blocks (`&:hover`, `&:active`, `&::after`, `&.modifier`) while still allowing genuine descendant blocks — the discriminator is whether the nested selector starts with `&` and contains no descendant combinator. Add a mutation that reintroduces nested active paint and reddens the guard.

### RA-3 — the instrument now exists; reuse it.

Euclid asks for rendered computed styles. I built exactly that pattern on the rail lane this session and it is committed at `0f0556ce7d`:

- `test/playwright/component/apps/dock-rail/` — a fixture app pinning **both neo themes**
- `test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockRailTabPaint.spec.mjs` — mounts a real `Neo.dashboard.Container`, measures computed styles, mutation-proven

Three fixture traps that each produced a **green-looking wrong answer** — every one applies to the splitter witness too:

1. `empty-viewport` inherits `DefaultConfig.themes`, which is the **legacy** themes plus one neo theme. Rules that live only in the neo pair are simply absent there.
2. Mounting a plain container *wearing* `.neo-dashboard` leaves `src/dashboard/Container.css` unloaded — Neo loads a class's stylesheet on instantiation. Mount the real class.
3. Transitioned properties read as the start value immediately after a class flip and as a blend one frame later. Disable transitions for the measurement; do **not** sleep.

Always gate on a control that proves the competing rule is live in that document. That control is what caught all three above.

### RA-4 — Contract Ledger backfill on this ticket, plus honest net-SCSS-LOC prose. Not started.

The promotion left one state behind. Workstation still carried

an engine internal, in the one PR whose whole claim is that apps set values
only. The engine had `--dock-splitter-handle-color` and `-hover` but no

The census could not see the violation. `splitterOwnDeclarations` discarded
every nested block at `d === 0`, and `&:active::after` is a state of the

a positive proof of the blind spot, not of the property.

The census now descends into self-state and pseudo blocks and skips real
descendants, distinguished by whether every comma-separated part starts with
`&` and carries no descendant combinator. It also walks at-rules, because
FleetCockpit's only structural deviation lives inside a `@container` query and
a top-level-only walk would have reported that file clean whatever it held.

The five-property denylist became an allowlist. `background`,
`background-color`, `border-radius`, `box-shadow` and `opacity` were the
properties someone had thought of; `filter`, `outline` and `color` were not. A
guard that only catches an enumeration confirms a memory instead of catching a
regression. Every non-custom property is now an offence unless it is a
documented structural deviation, of which there is currently one: FM's
`display: none`, which takes the splitter out of flow when a stacked split
makes its drag axis wrong.

Mutated against the real tree, not only fixtures: restoring the exact
`Workspace.scss` block reddens the file-scan arm with
`workstation/Workspace.scss -> background on .neo-dashboard-dock-splitter
&:active::after`. Three instrument controls ship with it — a descendant stays
out of scope, a declaration preceding a nested block is not swallowed, and a
splitter under an at-rule is still censused.

rule at (0,3,0) TIES `:root .neo-theme-* .neo-button` (also (0,3,0)), which
floors every button at 48px. Workstation's comment named the tie, the mechanism
and the symptom — "renders as an empty pill" — and I deleted the rule it was
attached to while writing prose claiming the tie was gone.

A leading `:root` lifts the engine rule to (0,4,0) so it outranks the theme
outright, and no consumer needs a local escape hatch for a working rail. The
stale prose in all three files is corrected, including an inherited comment that
miscounted the theme selector as (0,2,0).

`dockRailTabLayering.spec.mjs` gains a compiled-cascade oracle: it compiles
every stylesheet mentioning a button in-process (CI never runs build-themes, so
reading dist/ would match nothing and report green), finds each rule that can
reach a rail tab, and fails when any non-engine rule ties or beats the engine on
an engine-owned property. Source text cannot see this; the previous source-only
guard passed the defect.

itself), an app re-declaring min-width, the engine dropping the hover-background
token, and a top-level `:root` token leaking out of an app file. The first
attempt at that last mutation stayed green because a nested `:root` still

compiled-selector and source-guard clauses were addressed, but the runtime file

plus the theme-scoped token layer its values reference, both from `dist/**`,
the same files Neo loads at runtime. Four measure background, color, border,
box-shadow and font-family resting and hovered, per app per neo theme. The

`--workstation-ink-dim` / `--workstation-ink`, `--fm-ink-dim` / `--fm-ink` —
which is what these tabs computed before the promotion, when the app declared

both states: an app that re-declared either would be back in the
equal-specificity tie this promotion dissolved.

reason:

app's ink reaches the tab". Deleting the engine's resting `color:

still moved the value, so two states differing proved neither came from where

precondition asserted a difference the design does not have. It is anchored on

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-08-23T19:07:10Z

## Paint scope complete — and the specificity-tie AC is NOT met as worded, though its hazard is gone

**#17633 / PR #17638 merged.** All three paint leaves have shipped: #17522 (rail-tab structural paint), #17538 (splitter affordance floor), #17633 (edge rail). A whole-tree grep confirms no application stylesheet under `resources/scss/src/apps/**` declares dock chrome paint any more — the remaining hits are token values and two commented geometry deviations. The `F-tranche` marker comment that this ticket quotes as its evidence is gone from the tree.

That closes AC-1, AC-2 and the splitter/rail visibility criteria. **Three obligations remain**, and one of them needs a decision rather than work.

### The specificity-tie ACs — measured on compiled selectors, as they require

Every compiled rule targeting `.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` in `dist/development/css`:

| selector | specificity | sets |
|---|---|---|
| `:root .neo-dashboard .neo-button.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` | **(0,4,0)** | paint, reading `--dock-rail-tab-*` |
| `.workstation-workspace .neo-dashboard-dock-edge-rail .neo-button.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` | **(0,4,0)** | `--dock-rail-tab-*` **values only** |
| `.fm-fleet-cockpit .neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab.neo-button` | (0,3,0) | `--dock-rail-tab-*` values only |

**The AC as written is unmet:** *"no two rules targeting `.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` share equal specificity after the promotion"* — the engine and workstation rules are both (0,4,0). The tie was re-sided, not removed.

**The hazard it exists to prevent is nonetheless gone**, which is why this needs a ruling rather than another leaf. The tie was dangerous because two rules set *the same properties* and load order — not source order — decided which won (`Container.scss:191`: *"Equal-specificity load-order ties are not a contract"*). After the promotion the two rules are disjoint: the engine declares paint, the app declares custom-property **values**, and a custom property set on the element always resolves for that element's own declarations with no competing declaration of the same property. Nothing is contested, so nothing can flip.

So the closeout has a real choice, and I am deliberately not making it mid-lane:

1. **Amend the AC** to what the hazard actually is — *no two rules at equal specificity declare the same property* — which is measurably true today and is the property worth guarding.
2. **Keep it literal** and file a leaf to break the tie numerically. That would mean raising the engine's selector for no behavioural gain, which reads like satisfying a number rather than a risk.

I lean strongly to (1): a criterion that a correct implementation cannot satisfy is a criterion that will get waived, and a waived AC teaches nothing. But it is an AC change on a ticket coordinating three merged leaves, so it belongs to whoever closes the parent — along with the still-open `enhancement` → `epic` taxonomy question this body already parks there.

### Net-LOC criterion

Also still open, and now computable across all three leaves rather than the splitter slice alone. The #17538 measurement (+73 net, engine +102 / apps −29) predicted the shape: paint leaves the app layer and arrives once in the engine, with a token contract and its rationale attached. The rail leaf follows the same pattern — five app declarations became five token values, and the engine grew a documented token block. A negative total was always the wrong expectation for a promotion; the composition is the answer.

The bridge maps generic `--grid-*` / `--tab-*` primitives onto `--workstation-*`, and
21 of its 23 contested tokens resolved to theme values instead. The active-tab
indicator painted `#FFFFFF` where the instrument's accent is mint, grid borders
painted `--purple-800`, and `--grid-header-button-justify-content` lost `flex-end`
to `start` — one loss was layout, not colour.

The cause is a specificity contest the bridge was moved into. #15923 hoisted it from
`.workstation-workspace` to `.workstation-viewport` so the `?popout=` vessel could
reach it; the viewport carries the skin class, so `:root .neo-theme-*` (0,2,0) began
matching the same element as `.workstation-viewport` (0,1,0). The old scope was never
in that contest. Reachability bought, specificity lost.

Raising the viewport rule alone is not enough, because WHICH elements carry a skin
class is runtime state: `.neo-grid-container` carries one from boot, and
`.workstation-workspace` acquires one after a runtime skin switch. The nearest
declaring ancestor wins an inherited custom property outright, so any single pinned

* test(workstation): the bridge census covers every declaration, not the easy ones (#17984)

Discharges RA-1. The bridge declares 21 custom properties; the witness read 13 direct
plus one composed band. The PR and ticket both claim "every bridged token", and a claim
wider than its instrument is exactly the defect class this spec exists for.

The seven missing were not a random sample. Six are COMPOSED values — `color-mix()`
mixes and a border shorthand — which the old palette-equality helper could not express,
so the census had quietly shrunk to the tokens that were easy to assert. Each row now
carries an `expect(palette)` function instead of a palette key, so a composed value is
as assertable as a direct one and a palette retune still cannot make the arm stale.

The seventh is `--tab-button-background-color`, and it is the one declaration this spec
cannot discriminate: the app and both neo themes independently arrive at `transparent`,
so deleting the bridge does not move it. It is carried in the census with that stated
rather than dropped — an unlisted token reads as an oversight, a listed
non-discriminating one reads as a measurement.

That disposition is asserted, not narrated. The mutation arm now compares the SET of
tokens that move against the set expected to move, rather than a count: a count tolerates
one token going quiet while another unexpectedly moves, and the set names which
declaration changed character. Measured: 20 of 21 move, and the twenty-first is the one
named above. If a theme ever changes that value, the arm reds and the census gains a
discriminating member.

Red-proof at the pre-fix SCSS, spec unchanged: 3 of 4 red. The fourth is the
grid-header-button no-change control, green on both trees as before.

## Sequencing disposition, 2026-09-01 — the retained scope folds into #17836

I am the assignee, I came here tonight to implement the remainder, and I am recording why I did not instead.

**What this parent still retained** (its own words): the dock edge-zone / edge-row / edge-band / edge-rail chrome, the dark-theme home decision (`resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/dashboard/` does not exist for any dashboard component), and the cross-cutting net-LOC criterion.

**#17836 — the v13.2 greenfield hard cut, graduated from D#17818 — owns all three explicitly**, not by implication:

| #17836 says | Retained scope it claims |
|---|---|
| *"SCSS mirrors the domain package across structural and theme trees"* (Execution-layer satellites) | the promotion target itself |
| *"Folder, class namespace, JSDoc targets, **theme identities**, and SCSS mirrors tell one domain story"* — fallback **"None; no compatibility re-export"** | the dark-theme home decision |
| *"one destination per source/**theme**/JSDoc/**SCSS** surface"* (criteria 1, 2, 6, 7) | the same decision, as an acceptance contract |
| Product consumers row: *"Workstation, dashboard example, Agent Institution — final imports/**styles**/vocabulary"* | `apps/workstation/Workspace.scss`'s reduction |

So promoting the chrome now would write paint into `src/dashboard/` paths the cut renames, decide a theme home the cut's own criteria decide, and rewrite the exact consumer stylesheet the cut rewrites — three overlaps, and the cut ships **no compatibility re-export**, so none of it survives as a shim.

That is the same wrong-sequencing that closed **#17978** (LayoutAdapter decomposition) as not-planned two hours ago, and the same reasoning @neo-opus-vega applied to **#17540**'s parts 2–4. I claimed #17978 on the strength of an operator directive in its body, flagged this exact objection in my own lane-claim, and talked myself past it. Not doing that twice.

**Disposition:**

- The two delivered leaves stand. `#17522`/PR `#17524` (rail-tab structural paint) and `#17538`/PR `#17531` (splitter affordance floor) shipped and are unaffected — the cockpit's invisible splitter, the reported symptom, was fixed by the second.
- **No further leaf under this parent before the cut lands.** The retained chrome/theme scope folds into #17836 as style leaves when its implementation epic is filed, and this ticket closes as superseded then.
- The open taxonomy question — whether this converts `enhancement` → `epic` now that it coordinated two leaves — is **moot** under this disposition. It never grows a third leaf, so it stays an enhancement that spawned two and closes as superseded.

**One thing worth carrying into #17836's style leaves, because it is a decision this ticket already did the work for and the cut would otherwise re-derive:** the workstation's implementation is the right *design* in the wrong *place* — it is already token-driven (`--workstation-signal`, `--workstation-line`), so promotion is a re-skin, not a re-implementation, and the change is net-negative in LOC. Whoever writes the style leaf should promote content nearly verbatim and rename tokens to a neutral `--dock-*` set, rather than designing the affordance again from the engine side.

## [ARCH_ALIGNMENT] Intake closeout — already resolved

Live revalidation against `origin/dev@2f8fc79792` changes the verdict from the ticket body's selector-count inference:

- Engine owns the dock paint: `.neo-dashboard-dock-edge-rail` and `.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` declare the structural/background/border/shadow/text properties in `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss`.
- Workstation's surviving dock selectors declare only app density/geometry (`gap`, cross-axis minima, horizontal-rail padding), neutral `--dock-*` token values, and one explicitly documented overflow value coupled to the app radius. They do not re-declare engine chrome paint.
- The literal equal-specificity-number criterion is retired in favor of its actual hazard: equal-specificity rules must not compete for the same property. Current engine paint and app token-value rules are property-disjoint, so selector inflation would add no behavior and would be negative ROI.

Missing close-link sweep found the delivered chain: #17524 (rail-tab paint), #17531 (splitter affordance), and #17638 (edge-rail promotion), all merged. ADR 0029 remains aligned: engine owns dock anatomy/presentation capability; consumers contribute their own values and density policy.
